{{Short description|Swedish physicist (1922–2017)}}
[[File:John Adams, CERN Director General, and Gösta Ekspong, Chair of the CERN Scientific Policy Committee.jpg|thumb|John Adams, CERN Director General, and Gösta Ekspong, Chair of the CERN Scientific Policy Committee.]]
'''Anders ''Gösta'' Ekspong''' (born '''Anders Gösta Carlson'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://inspirehep.net/search?p=exactauthor%3AG.Ekspong.1&sf=earliestdate|title=List of publications for Gösta Ekspong|access-date=12 June 2018}}</ref> on 24 February 1922 in [[Skogstorp, Eskilstuna Municipality|Skogstorp]], [[:sv:Husby-Rekarne församling|Husby-Rekarne Township]], [[Södermanland County]], – 24 February 2017<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.familjesidan.se/system/funeral_notices/pdfs/000/780/797/original/1562876-1.pdf?1488686567|title=Funeral notice for Gösta Ekspong|language=Swedish}}</ref>) was a Swedish physicist and former professor at [[Stockholm University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Ekspong_G%C3%B6sta|title=Academy of Europe: Ekspong Gösta|last=Hoffmann|first=Ilire Hasani, Robert|website=www.ae-info.org|access-date=2018-06-12}}</ref> His main area of work was [[atomic physics]]. Ekspong defended his thesis for doctorate in 1955 at [[Uppsala University]] with a dissertation on [[Cosmic radiation|Cosmic Radiation]] under supervision of [[:sv:Axel E. Lindh|Axel E. Lindh]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Ekspong|first=A. G.|title=Some properties of the soft component of cosmic radiation|url=http://inspirehep.net/record/1650090}}</ref>

Ekspong is considered to be one of the Swedish pioneers in the involvement of the particle physics laboratory at [[CERN]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fysik.su.se/blog/vi-minns-gosta-ekspong/|title=Vi minns Gösta Ekspong|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170913005751/http://www.fysik.su.se/blog/vi-minns-gosta-ekspong/|language=Swedish|access-date=12 June 2018|archive-date=2017-09-13}}</ref> At CERN, he was chairman of the Emulsion Experiments Committee from the early 1960s<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|date=2017-06-01|title=Faces and places|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/2268963|journal=CERN Courier|volume=57}}</ref> as well as member of the Scientific Policy Committee (1969-1975),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://council.web.cern.ch/en/content/membership-scientific-policy-committee|title=Membership of the Scientific Policy Committee {{!}} CERN Council|website=council.web.cern.ch|access-date=2018-06-12}}</ref> where he also spent two years as chairman (1972-1974).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://council.web.cern.ch/en/content/chairs-scientific-policy-committee|title=Chairs of the Scientific Policy Committee {{!}} CERN Council|date=2017-10-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025222336/https://council.web.cern.ch/en/content/chairs-scientific-policy-committee|access-date=2018-06-12|archive-date=2017-10-25}}</ref> He made a significant contribution to the search strategies that would later be used in the search of the [[Higgs boson]] and participated in the technological development of [[DELPHI experiment|DELPHI]].<ref name=":0" /> Ekspong was elected as a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in 1969. From 1975 to 1988 he was also a member of the [[Nobel Committee for Physics]] where he held the post of chairman between 1987 and 1988. During his career Ekspong published several scientific publications regarding subjects such as [[particle physics]], [[astrophysics]] and [[nuclear physics]], some together with researchers at the [[University of Bristol]] and the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/articles/ekspong/cv.html|title=CV of Gösta Ekspong|date=2008-06-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080622154445/http://nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/articles/ekspong/cv.html|access-date=2018-06-12|archive-date=2008-06-22}}</ref> He is currently buried at [[Skogskyrkogården]] in [[Stockholm]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.svenskagravar.se/gravsatt/57880752|title=Svenska Gravar, Anders Gösta Ekspong|language=Swedish|access-date=12 June 2018}}</ref>
